plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
This strategy prioritizes income and broad index exposure.
Maintain a significant cash buffer for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to reduce overall leverage.
Buy NVDD at 4% as a strong scanner long setup to add quality tech exposure.
This balances broad index and quality tech with a small amount of leverage.
Maintain a cash buffer of approximately 10%.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets risk-first growth, aiming for ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to press working positions.
Buy NVDD at 6% as a strong scanner long setup, leaning into high-scoring opportunities.
This strategy uses leverage and concentration for stretch growth.
Maintain strict stop discipline due to amplified risk and daily decay of leveraged ETFs.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4% per month. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown potential and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged single names (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to near zero.
Add QQQI to 30% to increase exposure to income-generating ETFs.
This strategy prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
Keep a cash buffer for stability, understanding distributions are variable.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting ~1% per month. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff.
